sermon.title: What Overcomes You Makes You a Slave
sermon.speaker: Unidentified speaker (not clearly Pastor Kincer)
sermon.summary: A short message comparing Israel’s bondage in Egypt to slavery to sin. Whoever commits sin is a slave of sin, but the Son sets you free now, not only for heaven; worship and prayer are tools that bring us to Christ, and the world’s promise of freedom only makes slaves.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Short excerpt (about 5 minutes). He says God planned two years from Egypt to the promised land (commonly an eleven-day journey per Deuteronomy 1:2); kept as said. He cites Peter “chapter 2:18” (2 Peter 2:18–19).

faqs.question: Where did Jacob’s family live in Egypt?
How did the Egyptians treat Israel?
faqs.answer: With rigor; they made their lives bitter with hard bondage in mortar and brick.

scriptures.text_nkjv: So the Egyptians made the children of Israel serve with rigor. And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage—in mortar, in brick, and in all manner of service in the field. All their service in which they made them serve was with rigor.

faqs.question: How does sin take hold?
faqs.answer: It starts in your mind, grows into coveting while you don’t stop it, and then comes out and you’ve committed it.

faqs.question: Who said whoever commits sin is a slave of sin?
faqs.answer: Christ, in red letters in John 8:34.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus answered them, “Most assuredly, I say to you, whoever commits sin is a slave of sin.

faqs.question: Do worship and fasting set us free?
faqs.answer: No; they are tools God uses to bring you to Jesus Christ, who sets you free.

faqs.question: Is it what we do that saves us?
faqs.answer: No, it is Christ that saves you; be careful not to give credit to ourselves.

faqs.question: How does the world sell sin?
faqs.answer: Advertisements say this is freedom and fun; come on, just pay the money.

faqs.question: Can Christians be enslaved?
faqs.answer: Yes; Israel believed in God and prayed, and we can be enslaved as Christians, so we need God to bring us out.
